title: Stoics and Epicureans
objective: After this level you can compare two Greek schools about how to live well.
summary: Around 300 BCE two schools opened in Athens: Zeno’s Stoics said virtue is the only good; Epicurus said the goal is pleasure, meaning freedom from pain and worry.

cards.headline: Around 300 BCE, two schools opened in Athens: one on a porch, one in a garden.
cards.body: Both asked the same question: how do you live well? Their answers could hardly be more different.

cards.headline: The porch
cards.body: Zeno of Citium came to Athens about 312 BCE and taught in the Stoa Poikile, the Painted Porch; his followers were named Stoics after it. Their core claim: virtue is the only true good. Live in harmony with nature, guided by reason. Strong emotions, they held, are errors of judgment, so reason can correct them. Stuck in traffic? A Stoic would say the traffic isn’t the problem; your judgment about it is.

cards.headline: The garden
cards.body: Epicurus opened his school, the Garden, in Athens around 306 BCE, and it admitted women and enslaved people. He called pleasure the goal of life, but defined it as the absence of pain in the body and trouble in the soul. His school lived mainly on barley bread and water. In one letter he asked for a little pot of cheese, so he could have a feast. Wild times.

items.label: Stoics
points: Virtue is the only true good
Emotions are errors reason can fix

cards.headline: Porch to palace
cards.body: Stoicism went on to win famous followers in the Roman world: the statesman Seneca, the former slave Epictetus and the emperor Marcus Aurelius. An idea taught on a porch in Athens ended up with an emperor and a former slave among its champions.

questions.prompt: Where does the name of the Stoic school come from?

options.label: A Greek word for enduring pain
options.rationale: The name comes from a place.

options.label: The Stoa Poikile, the Painted Porch where Zeno taught
A Spartan general named Stoa
options.rationale: The name comes from a place.

questions.explanation: Zeno taught in the Stoa Poikile, the Painted Porch, and his followers were named Stoics after it.

questions.prompt: What did Epicurus mean by the pleasure he called the goal of life?

options.label: Feasting and drinking as much as possible
options.rationale: His school lived on bread and water.

options.label: The absence of pain in the body and trouble in the soul
Winning fame and power in politics
options.rationale: Fame wasn’t his idea of pleasure.

questions.explanation: Epicurus defined pleasure as the absence of pain in the body and trouble in the soul, and lived on bread and water.

questions.prompt: Zeno came to Athens about 312 BCE. In Level 1’s timeline, which era of Greek history was that?
questions.explanation: The Hellenistic age ran from Alexander’s death in 323 BCE to 30 BCE, so 312 BCE falls inside it.
